learn.title: Terms and degree
learn.body: A polynomial is a sum of terms like $4x^3$, $-x$ and 2. The number in front is the coefficient. The degree is the highest exponent. Like terms have the same variable and exponent.

learn.title: Subtract $(5x^2+3x-2)-(2x^2-x+4)$
learn.body: Change every sign in the second bracket.
Only the coefficients change when you combine like terms. $2x+3x=5x$, not $5x^2$.

questions.explanation: The degree is the highest exponent of the variable.

questions.prompt: Which term is a like term of $3x^2$?
questions.explanation: Like terms have the same variable raised to the same power.
Add the coefficients: $2+3=5$. The $x$ stays as it is.

questions.prompt: In the same sum, what is the coefficient of $x$?
When you subtract a polynomial, \_\_ the sign of every term in it.
questions.explanation: The minus sign multiplies every term inside the brackets.

questions.prompt: In that difference, what is the coefficient of $x$?
Subtract $(2x+5)-(x+1)$. Put the steps in order.
steps: Change the signs of the second polynomial: $2x+5-x-1$
questions.explanation: Distribute the minus sign first, or you will subtract only the first term.
